name: mitre-attck-detection-catalog
description: Curated SOCForge detection catalog: 25 high-priority MITRE ATT&CK techniques with associated detection patterns, rule templates, data sources, and replay dataset references. Use as a ground-truth reference for detection rule validation and coverage gap analysis.

techniques.description: Adversaries attempt to access credential material stored in the process memory of the Local Security Authority Subsystem Service (LSASS). Tools like Mimikatz, ProcDump, and comsvcs.dll are commonly used.
detection_patterns: Process accessing lsass.exe memory with PROCESS_VM_READ
Execution of mimikatz.exe, procdump.exe with lsass target
comsvcs.dll MiniDump invocation via rundll32.exe
Unusual handle to lsass.exe from non-system processes
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: LSASS Memory Access
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_access
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetImage|endswith: '\lsass.exe'
    GrantedAccess|contains:
      - '0x1010'
      - '0x1410'
  condition: selection
level: critical
techniques.false_positive_notes: Antivirus and EDR processes legitimately access lsass.exe. Whitelist known security tools.

techniques.description: Adversaries misuse PowerShell for execution of malicious commands, often with encoded payloads (-EncodedCommand), hidden windows (-w hidden), and policy bypass (-ep bypass).
detection_patterns: powershell.exe with -EncodedCommand or -enc flag
powershell.exe -w hidden or -WindowStyle Hidden
PowerShell with -ep bypass or -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
IEX (Invoke-Expression) with DownloadString or WebClient
Base64-encoded command blocks
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Suspicious PowerShell Command Flags
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-EncodedCommand'
      - '-enc'
      - '-ep bypass'
      - 'IEX'
      - 'DownloadString'
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: IT automation scripts legitimately use encoded commands. Baseline known-good scripts.

techniques.description: Adversaries use WMI for lateral movement, remote execution, and persistence. wmic.exe process call create is a common pattern.
detection_patterns: wmic.exe process call create with remote node
WMI subscriptions created for persistence (EventFilter + EventConsumer)
PowerShell Invoke-WmiMethod or Get-WmiObject for remote exec
mofcomp.exe compiling MOF files for WMI subscription
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: WMI Remote Execution
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\wmic.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'process call create'
      - '/node:'
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: IT management tools (SCCM, Ansible) use WMI. Correlate with authorized change windows.

techniques.description: Adversaries establish persistence using WMI event subscriptions that trigger malicious payloads on system events.
detection_patterns: New WMI FilterToConsumerBinding creation
CommandLineEventConsumer with suspicious scripts
mofcomp.exe executing attacker-controlled MOF files
ActiveScriptEventConsumer creation
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: WMI Persistence via Event Subscription
status: test
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: wmi
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 5861
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Some endpoint management solutions use WMI subscriptions for legitimate monitoring.

techniques.description: Adversaries create scheduled tasks for persistence and lateral execution, often disguising them as legitimate Windows tasks.
detection_patterns: schtasks.exe /create with suspicious executables
Task XML creation in C:\Windows\System32\Tasks
Scheduled task pointing to temp or user profile paths
Task created with SYSTEM privileges from non-admin process
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Suspicious Scheduled Task Creation
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\schtasks.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/create'
  filter:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'C:\Windows\'
      - 'C:\Program Files\'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: Legitimate software creates scheduled tasks during installation. Filter by known software publishers.

techniques.description: Adversaries abuse mshta.exe to execute malicious HTA scripts or VBScript, bypassing application whitelisting.
detection_patterns: mshta.exe loading remote URLs (http:// or https://)
mshta.exe spawning suspicious child processes
mshta.exe executed from Office macros
HTA files with embedded vbscript loading payloads
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Mshta Loading Remote Payload
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\mshta.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'http://'
      - 'https://'
      - 'vbscript'
      - 'javascript'
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Rarely used legitimately in enterprise environments. High-confidence indicator.

techniques.description: Adversaries attempt a small number of commonly used passwords against many accounts to avoid lockout thresholds.
detection_patterns: Multiple failed logon events (4625) across distinct accounts from single source
Failed logons with same password across many accounts within time window
Logon failures with Logon Type 3 (Network) from external IPs
Azure AD sign-in failures across many UPNs
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Password Spray via Failed Logons
status: test
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4625
    LogonType: 3
  timeframe: 5m
  condition: selection | count() by TargetUserName > 10
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Misconfigured applications or expired password sync can generate bursts. Correlate with source IP reputation.

techniques.description: Adversaries encrypt victim files to deny access. Ransomware uses high-entropy file writes, mass file renaming, and creation of ransom notes.
detection_patterns: Mass file extension changes within short time window
Process with high file rename/write rate
Unknown process writing high-entropy data to multiple files
Ransom note filenames (HOW_TO_DECRYPT.txt, README_RANSOM.txt)
Shadow copy deletion immediately before encryption
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Ransomware Ransom Note Creation
status: test
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|contains:
      - 'HOW_TO_DECRYPT'
      - 'README_RANSOM'
      - 'RESTORE_FILES'
      - 'YOUR_FILES'
  condition: selection
level: critical
techniques.false_positive_notes: None expected. Ransom note filename patterns are highly specific.

techniques.description: Adversaries delete shadow copies, backup catalogs, and disable recovery mechanisms before or during ransomware deployment.
detection_patterns: vssadmin.exe delete shadows
wbadmin.exe delete catalog
bcdedit.exe /set recoveryenabled no
PowerShell Get-WmiObject Win32_ShadowCopy | Remove-WmiObject
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Shadow Copy Deletion
status: stable
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_vss:
    Image|endswith: '\vssadmin.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'delete'
      - 'shadows'
  selection_bcdedit:
    Image|endswith: '\bcdedit.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: 'recoveryenabled'
  condition: 1 of selection_*
level: critical
techniques.false_positive_notes: Legitimate backup solutions occasionally manage shadow copies. Correlate with authorized maintenance windows.

techniques.technique_name: Indicator Removal: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.description: Adversaries clear event logs to remove evidence of malicious activity. wevtutil, PowerShell Clear-EventLog, and direct log file deletion are common methods.
detection_patterns: wevtutil cl Security / System / Application
PowerShell Clear-EventLog cmdlet
Windows Event 1102 (audit log cleared)
Windows Event 104 (System log cleared)
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Windows Event Log Cleared
status: stable
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID:
      - 1102
      - 104
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Log rotation tools may trigger 104. Correlate with user account and time of day.

techniques.description: Adversaries communicate with C2 infrastructure using HTTP/HTTPS to blend with legitimate web traffic.
detection_patterns: Low-frequency periodic HTTP/HTTPS beaconing to unknown external IPs
HTTP connections to IP addresses (no domain) over port 80/443
Unusual User-Agent strings in web proxy logs
JA3/JA3S TLS fingerprint mismatches for known software
Domain generation algorithm (DGA) suspicious domains
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: C2 HTTP Beaconing to IP Address
status: test
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    c-uri-query: ''
    cs-host|re: '^(?:[0-9]{1,3}\.){3}[0-9]{1,3}$'
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: Some software communicates with IP addresses directly. Whitelist known CDNs and update servers.

techniques.description: Adversaries use DNS to exfiltrate data or communicate with C2 via DNS tunneling, often using long subdomains or high query volume.
detection_patterns: DNS queries with unusually long subdomains (>50 chars)
High-volume DNS queries to single domain
DNS TXT record queries from endpoints
DNS queries to recently registered domains (< 30 days)
Beaconing pattern in DNS query timestamps
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: DNS Tunneling via Suspicious Query Length
status: test
logsource:
  category: dns
detection:
  selection:
    QueryName|re: '^[a-zA-Z0-9]{50,}\.'
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: CDN domains and some cloud services have long subdomains. Correlate with query frequency and destination reputation.

techniques.description: Adversaries obtain and use legitimate credentials to gain access, avoid detection, and maintain persistence.
detection_patterns: Logon from unusual geographic location for account
Off-hours logon for account that normally works 9-5
Account logging into systems it has never accessed before
Multiple accounts using same source IP within short window
Privileged account used interactively on non-admin workstation
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Admin Account Interactive Logon on Workstation
status: test
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 10
    TargetUserName|contains: 'admin'
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: IT admins legitimately use admin accounts. Baseline normal behavior and alert on deviations.

techniques.description: Adversaries collect data from network shares before exfiltration. Large-scale reads from file servers outside of normal patterns indicate collection activity.
detection_patterns: High volume file access from single account exceeding baseline
File access across multiple department shares not in user's normal pattern
Bulk read operations from sensitive share paths (Finance, HR, Executive)
Access to shares via unusual process (cmd.exe, powershell.exe)
Off-hours bulk file access
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Bulk File Access from Network Share
status: test
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 5145
    ShareName|contains:
      - 'Finance'
      - 'HR'
      - 'Executive'
      - 'Confidential'
  timeframe: 10m
  condition: selection | count() by SubjectUserName > 100
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Backup jobs access many files. Correlate with service account vs. user account and time of activity.

techniques.description: Data is exfiltrated to removable USB drives. DLP solutions should alert on large file writes to removable media.
detection_patterns: Large file write to removable media drive letter
USB storage device inserted by unexpected user
File copy to drive:\ with suspicious file extensions
DLP policy violation on removable media write
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Large File Write to USB Drive
status: test
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|re: '^[E-Z]:\\'
    FileSize|gt: 104857600
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: IT administrators may use USB drives for imaging. Correlate with authorized device inventory.

techniques.description: Adversaries exfiltrate data to cloud storage services (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, Box) to blend with legitimate cloud traffic.
detection_patterns: Large HTTPS upload to personal cloud storage domains
Personal cloud storage access from corporate endpoint
Unusual upload volume to cloud storage outside business hours
Cloud storage upload from DLP-flagged data origin
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Data Exfiltration to Personal Cloud Storage
status: test
logsource:
  category: proxy
detection:
  selection:
    cs-method: 'PUT'
    cs-host|contains:
      - 'drive.google.com'
      - 'api.dropbox.com'
      - 'api.box.com'
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Authorized corporate OneDrive/SharePoint usage is legitimate. Block personal cloud services via CASB.

techniques.description: Adversaries achieve persistence by adding malicious entries to registry Run keys or the startup folder.
detection_patterns: Registry modification to HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
Registry modification to HKCU\...\Run pointing to temp/appdata paths
File creation in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup
reg.exe add with RunOnce key
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Registry Run Key Modification
status: stable
logsource:
  category: registry_set
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains:
      - '\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
      - '\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\RunOnce'
  filter:
    Details|contains:
      - 'C:\Program Files'
      - 'C:\Windows'
  condition: selection and not filter
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: Many legitimate applications use Run keys. Focus on executables in user-writable paths.

techniques.technique_name: Impair Defenses: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.description: Adversaries disable security tools such as Windows Defender, antivirus, and firewalls to enable undetected activity.
detection_patterns: Set-MpPreference -Disable* $true via PowerShell
netsh advfirewall set allprofiles state off
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows Defender\DisableAntiSpyware = 1
Termination of security processes (MsMpEng.exe, SentinelOne, CrowdStrike)
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Windows Defender Disabled via PowerShell
status: stable
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'Set-MpPreference'
      - 'DisableRealtimeMonitoring'
  condition: selection
level: critical
techniques.false_positive_notes: Penetration testing tools may disable AV during authorized engagements. Verify with change management.

techniques.technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
techniques.description: Adversaries compress and archive collected data using utilities like 7-Zip, WinRAR, or Tar to reduce size and enable exfiltration.
detection_patterns: 7z.exe, WinRAR.exe, or tar.exe with password flag (-p)
Archive creation in temp directories or user profile paths
Archives created from sensitive share paths
Compression of large data volumes in unusual locations
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Suspicious Archive with Password
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\7z.exe'
      - '\WinRAR.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '-p'
      - '-hp'
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: IT creates password-protected archives routinely. Correlate with file origin and destination.

techniques.description: Adversaries scan the network for open ports and running services to identify targets for lateral movement.
detection_patterns: nmap, masscan, or PortScan.exe execution
High volume of TCP SYN packets to multiple internal hosts
Port scanning from workstation to server subnet
PowerShell Test-NetConnection in loops
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Internal Network Port Scan
status: test
logsource:
  category: network_connection
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Initiated: 'true'
  timeframe: 1m
  condition: selection | count() by SourceIp > 50
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: Vulnerability scanners (Nessus, Qualys) generate similar patterns. Whitelist scanner IPs.

techniques.description: Adversaries create local accounts for persistence, often adding them to local Administrators group.
detection_patterns: net user /add command execution
Windows Event 4720 (user account created)
New account added to local Administrators (Event 4732)
PowerShell New-LocalUser cmdlet
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Local Account Created
status: stable
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4720
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: Service account creation during software installation triggers this. Correlate with expected deployment windows.

techniques.technique_name: Use Alternate Authentication Material: Pass the Hash
techniques.description: Adversaries authenticate using stolen NTLM password hashes without knowing the plaintext password.
detection_patterns: NTLM authentication with account that normally uses Kerberos
Logon Event 4624 with Logon Type 3 and NTLM auth from anomalous source
Mimikatz sekurlsa::pth execution
Overpass-the-hash producing Kerberos ticket from NTLM hash
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Pass the Hash via Unusual NTLM Logon
status: test
logsource:
  product: windows
  service: security
detection:
  selection:
    EventID: 4624
    LogonType: 3
    AuthenticationPackageName: 'NTLM'
    WorkstationName: ''
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Legacy applications using NTLM are common. Correlate with source host and account role.

techniques.description: Adversaries obfuscate malicious files, scripts, or payloads to evade detection. Encoded PowerShell, XOR'd shellcode, and packed binaries are common techniques.
detection_patterns: High-entropy file content in script files
Base64 encoded content in script blocks
Files with PE headers in renamed/obfuscated extensions
PowerShell -EncodedCommand with long base64 strings
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Highly Encoded PowerShell Command
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\powershell.exe'
    CommandLine|base64offset|contains: 'IEX'
  condition: selection
level: high
techniques.false_positive_notes: Some legitimate software uses base64 encoding for configuration. Validate with code signing status.

techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate domain trust relationships to identify targets across trusted domains for lateral movement.
detection_patterns: nltest.exe /domain_trusts
PowerShell Get-ADTrust cmdlet
netdom query /domain
Enumeration of external trust relationships
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Domain Trust Discovery via Nltest
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\nltest.exe'
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '/domain_trusts'
      - '/all_trusts'
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: IT administrators legitimately run domain trust queries during troubleshooting. Rarely in automated scripts.

techniques.description: Adversaries enumerate domain groups (especially privileged ones like Domain Admins) to identify targets for privilege escalation.
detection_patterns: net group "Domain Admins" /domain
PowerShell Get-ADGroupMember for privileged groups
LDAP queries for group membership from non-admin accounts
Bulk AD group enumeration
techniques.sigma_rule_template:
title: Domain Admin Group Enumeration
status: test
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Image|endswith: '\net.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'group'
      - 'Domain Admins'
  condition: selection
level: medium
techniques.false_positive_notes: Help desk and IT staff enumerate domain groups routinely for access provisioning.
